newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal pilots suspend strike as TAP seeks deal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal pilots suspend strike as TAP seeks deal.

text.p: Pilots at struggling Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal on Monday suspended a series of selective strikes to give time to reach a deal with the company on working hours.

Planning Minister Joao Cravinho told reporters that the pilots, who had been refusing to fly flights not scheduled at least three days in advance, had called off their action for five days to let talks continue.
Cravinho, who chaired negotiations between the company and pilots late on Sunday, said that five days should be sufficient to work out an accord on flight scheduling, which pilots say is chaotic.
"The five days were set by the union and with the experience that they have of these things, they must have thought that it was sufficient time for an agreement to be reached," Cravinho said.
The stoppages, which had begun on Saturday, were due to continue throughout August in a move that TAP said could provoke heavy losses for the company during the peak holiday season.
Company officials said on Sunday that the pilots' action had caused 11 flights to be cancelled since it began shortly before midnight on Saturday.
The airline only flies international routes and to Portugal's Atlantic Azores and Madeira islands.
The government had warned that the pilots' action was risking the survival of the airline, which hoped to return profit in 1997 after years of losses.
It says that it is barred by agreements with the European Union from pouring any more funds into the company, which it hopes to privatise, at least partially, before the end of the century.
